tally.headline: 4 of 10 gradeable claims held up, 4 did not

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 2.7 points toward Washington Commanders of the quote EdgeDesk captured at DraftKings. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 42.4 sat 4.1 points below the captured total of 46.5.

closing_line.why: no closing line is held for this game: the Collective captured none and the schedule feed carries none. Closing-line value is left blank rather than estimated from the result.

reasons: 4 of 8 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 1.2 and the game finished 17 the home way — 15.8 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

verdict.line: THE NUMBER LANDED AND THE REASONING DID NOT. This is the most dangerous result on this page, because it pays and teaches nothing. Nothing below should be read as EdgeDesk having understood this game.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 4 of the claims in this article rested on model, home_field, matchup.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; home advantage is priced into the number and cannot be isolated from one game’s box score..
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, home_field, matchup.

lessons.actual_result: It graded a win. The reasoning behind it did not hold: 4 of 8 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
lessons.lesson: A winning number built on a reading the game contradicted. Nothing about this result should increase confidence in the mechanism EdgeDesk named, and treating it as confirmation is how a model gets worse while its record gets better.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Why did the number land while the mechanism failed? Either the number was right for a reason EdgeDesk has not identified, or it was luck. Both are worth knowing and they are different.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Washington Commanders −1.0 where the market has Washington Commanders +1.5 at DraftKings — a 2.7 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Washington Commanders won by 17. the result landed on EdgeDesk’s side of the market number: Washington Commanders beat a margin of -1.5
lessons.lesson: The disagreement landed. One landing proves nothing on its own; the aggregate of them, held against the closing line, is the only thing that would.
